name: agent-chef-mcp

tools.name: run_agent_chef
tools.description: The one call to make when the user says 'run agent chef' (or run the app / plan dinner / do the weekly thing). Returns the operating manual plus the checklist of tool calls that are due right now. Execute them in order, then call next_actions again until it returns no actions. Stop before any checkout.

tools.name: record_schedule
tools.description: Call after creating (or changing) the recurring 'Run Agent Chef.' task in your own scheduler, with a one-line description, e.g. 'Claude scheduled task, daily 9:00 and 18:00 America/Los_Angeles'. Lets the app stop reminding you and shows the owner that the loop is automated.

cleared.description: true if the schedule was removed

tools.name: dismiss_setup_checklist
tools.description: Hides the 'Get set up' card on the household dashboard (e.g. when the owner says they don't need it). Pass show=true to bring it back.

tools.name: get_connected_agents
tools.description: Agents connected to this household via OAuth sign-in (Claude, ChatGPT…), with when they connected and last used. API keys are separate.

tools.name: revoke_connected_agent
tools.description: Revoke an OAuth-connected agent's access (client_id from get_connected_agents). It must sign in again to reconnect.

tools.name: next_actions
tools.description: START HERE. Returns the current phase and an ordered checklist of tool calls that are due right now (propose, send ballot, remind non-voters, add options for feedback, lock in, shop), with why and the arguments/message text to use. Execute them, then call again until empty. Idempotent and time-aware; safe to call on a schedule.

tools.name: get_instructions
tools.description: The full operating manual for agents: the run loop, phases, how to write recipes, messaging and safety rules. Read once per session.

tools.name: get_recipe_preferences
tools.description: Household name, recipe preferences prompt (diet, allergies, dislikes, cuisines, time budget), shopping preferences prompt (brands, organic, store quirks) plus settings: plan_day, servings, grocery_store, recipes_per_week, votes_per_member.

tools.name: update_recipe_preferences
tools.description: Update any subset of the preferences prompt and settings. Omitted fields are unchanged.

vote_close_time.description: Local time voting closes, HH:MM 24h, e.g. 18:00

reminder_hours_before.description: Send non-voters one reminder this many hours before voting closes

preferences.description: Free-form prompt describing what the household likes/avoids. Replaces existing text.

shopping_preferences.description: Free-form prompt for the grocery run: preferred brands, organic when possible, substitutions, store quirks. Replaces existing text.

tools.name: get_members
tools.description: List household members with contact info, whether they have signed in to Agent Chef themselves (has_account), whether they get push notifications, and their personal vote links.

tools.name: upsert_member
tools.description: Add a household member, or edit one: name is the key (case-insensitive), or pass member_id from get_members to rename. Phone and email update when given; an empty string clears them. Use this when someone wants to add or fix a member's contact details; never remove and re-add, which breaks their vote link. Roles: member (default) can vote, rate and browse once they sign in; admin can also change settings, recipes and weeks like the owner.

member_id.description: Edit this member by id (from get_members); this is how you rename someone. Without it, name is the match key.

phone.description: E.164, e.g. +15551234567. An empty string clears it.

role.description: Only for members who have signed in to Agent Chef (has_account); admin needs an account

tools.name: remove_member
tools.description: Remove a household member by name (their votes and ratings stay attached to past weeks). The owner can't be removed.

tools.name: get_ingredients
tools.description: What the household already has, so the shopping list can skip it. Staples (staple: true) are always on hand unless marked out; leftovers carry expires_at and drop off on their own.

tools.name: update_ingredients
tools.description: Keep the pantry: add staples the household always has (omit days), add leftovers that should be skipped for a while and then drop off (days, 7 is typical), mark staples out when they run low so they go back on the shopping list, or remove items. Adding a staple that was out puts it back in stock. Don't add a week's groceries: they get cooked that week.

days.description: Leftover: skip it on shopping lists for this many days, then drop it. Omit for a staple.

out.description: Staples the household ran out of; they return to stock when an order includes them

tools.name: get_favorite_recipes
tools.description: Recipes marked as household favorites, with ratings. Good candidates to re-propose by recipe_id.

tools.name: favorite_recipe
tools.description: Mark (or unmark) a recipe as a household favorite.

tools.name: get_recipe
tools.description: Full details for one recipe: ingredients, steps, servings, source, tags, ratings, comments, how often it's been cooked, a link to its page, and a public share_url anyone can open.

tools.name: search_recipes
tools.description: Every recipe the household has ever had proposed, with ratings and cook counts. Filter by text, favorites, or tag. Use recipe_id from here with propose_recipes to re-propose.

scope.description: ours (default): this household's recipes. library: Community recipes, the shared pool of public recipes, with cooks/favorites/ratings across households. all: both.

tools.name: add_library_recipe
tools.description: Copy a recipe from Community recipes (search_recipes with scope 'library') into this household. Pass favorite: true to also mark it a favorite. Returns the household's copy; use its id on ballots. Passing a library id straight to propose_recipes or add_candidates does the same copy automatically.

tools.name: update_recipe
tools.description: Edit a stored recipe: fix an ingredient, add steps, change servings, tags, image or source, or set public to publish it on agentchef.net/recipes. Only provided fields change.

public.description: Publish this recipe on agentchef.net/recipes (indexable, with the household's name). Imported recipes show ingredients and link to the source for steps.

tools.name: import_recipe
tools.description: Fetch a recipe page (most cooking sites) and save it to the library with its real photo, ingredients, and steps. Returns the recipe; pass its recipe_id to propose_recipes or add_candidates to put it on a ballot.

annotations.title: Import a recipe from a URL

tools.name: create_recipe
tools.description: Save a recipe to the library from details you already have: one you read in your browser (when a site blocks import_recipe or has no recipe markup), one the owner dictated, or one you wrote. Provide the complete ingredient list with quantities and the steps; include the source page and a real photo URL when you have them. Optionally mark it a favorite.

image_url.description: A real, publicly reachable photo of the dish; verified by the server and dropped if dead

annotations.title: Save a recipe you already have

tools.name: set_recipe_image
tools.description: Store a photo for a recipe permanently and set it as the recipe's image. Use for images you generated with your image tool (their URLs expire) or any photo you have as a URL or base64. Pass either image_url (we fetch and copy it) or image_base64 + content_type. Max 6 MB; JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF.

annotations.title: Attach a photo to a recipe

tools.name: import_recipes
tools.description: Bulk version of import_recipe: fetch up to 15 recipe pages and save them to the library, optionally marking each as a favorite. Use when the owner is moving favorites from another app (Mealime, a meal kit, a recipe manager). Names without URLs are your job: search for a real recipe page first, then pass the URLs here. Per-URL failures are reported, not thrown.

favorite_all.description: Mark every imported recipe as a favorite

tools.name: get_past_recipes
tools.description: Every recipe selected for a past week, newest first, with week, status, and ratings/comments. Use to avoid repeats and learn what landed.

tools.name: get_current_week
tools.description: Where the cycle stands: latest week + status (voting/selected/ordered/done), candidates with tallies, who has/hasn't voted, selected recipes, pending_feedback. Call this first.

tools.name: propose_recipes
tools.description: Start a weekly cycle: store the candidate recipes (normally 10) and return numbered candidates, a ballot_text (with a {vote_link} placeholder for message_group), and each member's vote link. Re-calling for the same week_start replaces the candidates.

recipe_id.description: Reuse an existing recipe (e.g. a favorite) instead of providing details

description.description: One appetizing sentence, shown on the ballot

image_url.description: A real, publicly reachable photo of the dish: the og:image of the recipe page you used, or one found via web/image search. The server verifies the URL is an image and drops it otherwise. Never invent URLs; prefer import_recipe, which captures the source photo. For generated images use set_recipe_image afterwards.

ingredients.description: Complete list with quantities; drives the shopping list

tools.name: add_candidates
tools.description: Append extra recipes to the current voting ballot (positions continue after the existing ones; votes are kept; 15 max). Use in response to ballot_feedback from get_current_week; open feedback is marked addressed. Follow up with message_group so voters know new options are up.

recipe_id.description: Reuse an existing recipe (e.g. a favorite) instead of providing details

description.description: One appetizing sentence, shown on the ballot

image_url.description: A real, publicly reachable photo of the dish: the og:image of the recipe page you used, or one found via web/image search. The server verifies the URL is an image and drops it otherwise. Never invent URLs; prefer import_recipe, which captures the source photo. For generated images use set_recipe_image afterwards.

ingredients.description: Complete list with quantities; drives the shopping list

tools.name: add_ballot_feedback
tools.description: Record a member's comment about the current ballot (optionally about one candidate), e.g. relayed from a text message. Members can also do this themselves on their vote page.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Pass the owner's feedback about Agent Chef itself (a bug, a missing feature, something confusing) to the people who build it. Use when the owner says something like 'tell Agent Chef that…' or complains about the tool. Not for messages to the household.

contact.description: How to reach the owner for a reply, if they want one

tools.name: message_group
tools.description: Send a push notification, SMS/MMS or email to household members. '{vote_link}' in the message becomes each member's personal voting link. Channel 'auto' texts members with a phone and emails the rest. Providers now: {"sms":"dry-run","email":"resend","push":"web-push"} (dry-run = logged only).

channel.description: auto = push to members who opted in on their vote page, else text if they have a phone, else email

member_names.description: Limit to these members; default everyone

kind.description: What this message is; lets next_actions avoid repeats

tools.name: add_vote
tools.description: Record one member's votes for the current week (replaces their earlier votes). Accepts recipe_ids or ballot positions. Unknown member names are created.

tools.name: get_past_votes
tools.description: Historical ballots: per week, every candidate with vote count, voters, and whether it was selected.

tools.name: set_this_weeks_recipes
tools.description: Lock in the dinners. With no recipe_ids, picks the top N (recipes_per_week) by votes; a tie at the cutoff goes to the earlier ballot position and is reported under tie_break. With recipe_ids, those become the dinners exactly: any number, any household or Community recipe, on the ballot or not (off-ballot picks are added to the week). Call again to change them; an ordered week stays ordered. Moves a voting week to 'selected' and returns the shopping list.

tools.name: reopen_voting
tools.description: Undo set_this_weeks_recipes: clears the winners and returns the week to 'voting'. Existing votes are kept. Use if winners were locked in too early.

tools.name: set_voting_deadline
tools.description: One-off override of when the current ballot closes: an ISO timestamp, or extend_hours from the current deadline. Normally the deadline comes from the household schedule (vote_close_day/time); changing those via update_recipe_preferences re-syncs the current week.

tools.name: rate_recipe
tools.description: Record post-cook feedback (1-5 + comment) for one member. Every member rates separately; a member's newer rating replaces their older one. Ratings never change the week's status.

tools.name: assemble_online_grocery_order
tools.description: Returns the shopping list for filling an online grocery cart: everything this week's selected recipes need minus what is on hand, grouped by item with quantities and which recipe needs it, plus the preferred store. Drive the browser to fill the cart; stop before checkout for approval; then call record_grocery_order.

annotations.title: Get the shopping list for an online cart

tools.name: record_grocery_order
tools.description: Log the placed order and move the week to 'ordered'. Staples marked out that were bought are back in stock (listed under restocked). Purchased items don't join the pantry since they get cooked this week; set add_to_on_hand to keep them as leftovers for 7 days.

add_to_on_hand.description: Keep the purchased items as 7-day leftovers

instructions:
# How to run Agent Chef

You are the household's agent. Agent Chef is the state machine; you are the hands. You never need to remember where the week stands: the server tells you.

RUN LOOP. When the user says "run agent chef", call run_agent_chef (it returns this manual, today's checklist, and whether a recurring schedule exists) and follow it. The first time, also schedule yourself to run "Run Agent Chef." twice a day (09:00 and 18:00 in the household's timezone) and confirm it with record_schedule, so the whole week runs end to end without anyone asking. Then:
1. Call next_actions.
2. Execute the returned actions in order. Each one names the tool, why it's due, and the arguments or message text to use. Where an argument is in <angle brackets>, you fill it in (e.g. write the 10 recipes).
3. Call next_actions again. Repeat until it returns no actions, then stop and report a one-line summary.

THE PANTRY only exists to keep things off the shopping list. Staples are what the household always has (oil, salt, spices, rice): add them without days. Leftovers are what's around for now (half a bag of spinach): add them with days (7 is typical) and they drop off on their own. When someone says they ran out of a staple, mark it out with update_ingredients; it goes on the next list and is back in stock once an order includes it. Never add a week's groceries to the pantry.

WHAT THE PHASES MEAN
- new_cycle: it's past the household's plan day. Propose 10 recipes and send the ballot. Last week's unrated dinners are collected on the ballot page itself (a rating card sits above the new options), so don't send a separate rating request; the ballot text mentions it.
- voting: people vote on their personal links until voting_closes_at (household setting: weekday + time; set_voting_deadline moves it). You may be asked to send one reminder to non-voters shortly before the deadline, or to add 2-3 options answering ballot feedback. When everyone has voted or the deadline passes, lock in the winners, announce them, and build the cart. A tie at the cutoff is yours to break (next_actions names the tied dishes); the server's default is the earlier ballot position.
- The owner and admins have the final say. They can change the dinners at any time, in the app (Choose winners) or by asking you: pass their picks to set_this_weeks_recipes as recipe_ids, including recipes that were never on the ballot (household or Community ids). Winners marked admin_pick were chosen over the vote; don't second-guess them. If the dinners change after you announced them, announce the new list.
- shopping: assemble_online_grocery_order gives you the list minus the pantry plus the household's shopping_preferences (brands, organic, substitutions): follow them when picking products. Fill the cart in the store's website, show the total, and STOP for explicit approval before checkout. Then record_grocery_order.
- cooking / idle: nothing to do until the next plan day.

COMMUNITY RECIPES: Agent Chef has a shared pool of public recipes ("Community recipes") with photos, ingredients and steps, plus how many households cooked, favorited and rated each one. Before writing or importing recipes, call search_recipes with scope 'library' (a query or tag helps). Put library ids straight on the ballot with propose_recipes or add_candidates; the recipe is copied into the household automatically. add_library_recipe copies one into the household without putting it on a ballot (favorite: true also marks it a favorite). Prefer well-cooked, well-rated library recipes over untested ones from the web.

THE HOUSEHOLD'S OWN ROTATION comes first. Most families already have dinners they make on repeat, and they do not want a near-copy of one of them on the ballot or in the cart. Build most of the ballot from what the household already has (get_favorite_recipes, get_past_recipes, search_recipes scope 'ours'); new ideas are the minority, two or three unless the household asks for more. Before writing or importing a recipe, search_recipes scope 'ours' for the dish and use the existing recipe_id when there is one. When the owner describes their regular rotation, save it first (import_recipes for links, create_recipe for meals they make from memory), favorite those, and use them. The server guards this too: propose_recipes and add_candidates swap a new recipe for the household's own version when the title is the same dish (listed under 'replaced' in the result) and flag close matches under 'similar'. When you see either, tell the owner in one line and do not keep the duplicate.

WRITING RECIPES (propose_recipes / add_candidates): read get_recipe_preferences first, then search_recipes scope 'ours' so you build on what they already cook. Source recipes from real pages: import_recipe(url) saves a recipe from a trusted site with its photo, ingredients and steps, then pass its recipe_id; aim for most of the ballot to come from real sources. search_recipes finds anything already in the library. PHOTOS ARE YOUR JOB: every candidate should have a real image_url (the source page's photo, or one you found by searching). The server checks each URL is a live image and rejects dead ones; a card without a photo means you skipped this. If no real photo exists, generate one with your image tool (a realistic photo of the plated dish, natural light, no text, no people) and attach it with set_recipe_image, which stores it permanently; image-tool URLs expire, so never pass them as image_url directly. Photos copied from recipe sites stay private to the household; when a recipe is shared to Community recipes, only ingredients, a source link and an original photo are shown. After propose_recipes, check the returned candidates for a missing image_url and fix each with set_recipe_image. Use get_favorite_recipes (include 1-2), get_past_recipes (avoid repeats from the last ~4 weeks), get_past_votes (lean into what wins), get_ingredients (use what's on hand). Each recipe: title, one appetizing sentence, servings, complete ingredients with quantities, steps, tags, and a real image_url (see PHOTOS).

MESSAGING: message_group sends push notifications (to members who tapped "notify me" on their vote page), SMS or email, and personalises {vote_link} per person; channel auto picks push first, then text, then email. Pass the kind the action specifies so the server can track what was sent. If the household prefers, you may post the same text into their own group chat instead; still call message_group so it's logged (it dry-runs if no provider is configured).

SWITCHING FROM ANOTHER APP: when the owner lists meals they loved elsewhere (Mealime, a meal kit, a recipe manager), find a real recipe page for each name on a well-known recipe site, then save them all at once with import_recipes (favorite_all: true); URLs they give you go straight in. If you have a browser tool, you can collect the favorites yourself: open the old app, let the owner sign in (never type their password), gather the recipe links, then import. Mealime and HelloFresh recipe pages import cleanly; Blue Apron and Marley Spoon block automated fetching, so for those read each recipe card in your browser and save it with create_recipe (title, ingredients with quantities, steps, servings, photo URL, source link, favorite: true). Use create_recipe whenever import_recipe fails on a page you can read. Report what you saved and what you could not find. Favorites are re-proposed on future ballots.

ON-DEMAND REQUESTS: when the owner asks for something the schedule wouldn't do yet ("start next week's ballot now", "add two more options", "lock it in early", "send a reminder"), do it directly with the matching tool even if next_actions says nothing is due. For an early ballot, call propose_recipes with week_start set to the coming cycle start (next_actions returns it as on_demand / cycle_start) and then message_group with the ballot.

HOUSEHOLDS OF ONE work the same way: one voter, top N by their votes, same loop. Never block on adding members.

RULES: never invent a vote or a rating; never check out without explicit approval in this conversation; keep messages short and friendly; if a tool errors, fix the input and retry once, then report.
